articles.title: Brazos Concludes $4.4B Sale of Midland Basin Assets to ONEOK
articles.description: Brazos Midstream completed the divestment of its Midland Basin natural gas gathering and processing infrastructure to ONEOK for $4.425 billion.

articles.title: EIA Boosts Oil Price Forecast by $5 in 2026, $10 in 2027
articles.description: The U.S. Energy Information Administration raised its 2026 Brent crude oil spot price forecast by more than $5 per barrel and its 2027 Brent price forecast by $10 per barrel.

articles.title: Energy Transfer Buys Already Integrated Vaquero Assets for Over $2.6B
articles.description: Energy Transfer agreed to acquire Vaquero Midstream, whose assets are already interconnected with Energy Transfer's downstream natural gas and natural gas liquids infrastructure, for around $2.625 billion.

articles.title: India Shuns Costly Russian Oil
articles.description: Indian refiners have cut back Russian crude purchases for November delivery.

articles.title: Emera to Acquire Canadian Utilities for $10B
articles.description: Emera and Canadian Utilities have entered into what they say is the largest merger between two Canadian companies, based on an enterprise value of around $50.47 billion.

articles.title: Shell, Chevron, Oxy Issue Hurricane Isaias Updates
articles.description: Shell, Chevron, and Occidental Petroleum have all issued updates in response to Hurricane Isaias.

articles.title: Chevron Exits Hess Midstream as It Restructures Bakken, DJ Assets
articles.description: Hess Midstream will become independent of Chevron through a swap transaction that lets Chevron keep using oil and gas gathering and processing infrastructure in the Bakken at lower cost.

articles.title: Equinor raises Snøhvit Future cost forecast to $2.7bn
articles.description: Equinor has lifted the investment forecast for its Snøhvit Future development in Norway to Nkr26.5bn ($2.7bn) in 2026 value, representing the third upward revision since the project was sanctioned.

articles.title: Valaris secures $220m in contract awards and extensions
articles.description: Offshore drilling contractor Valaris has reported new contract awards and extensions amounting to an estimated $220m in contract backlog since its previous fleet status update in August 2026.

articles.title: Russian Oil Flows to India Plunge to 310,000 Bpd
articles.description: India is reducing its imports of crude oil from Russia, but mostly not because of the U.S. tariff threat for buying Russian oil. Economics have always been driving Indian refiners’ purchases, and the past few weeks haven’t been different. Russia is scaling back imports of Russian oil as the price of Russia’s flagship Urals grade loaded in the Baltic ports has jumped and now nearly equals the prices of Middle Eastern crudes, whose availability has increased in recent weeks as flows through the Strait of Hormuz have rebounded,…

articles.title: Equinor Finds New Gas at Norway’s 40-Year-Old Gullfaks Field
articles.description: Equinor has discovered gas at the Gullfaks field, which would help maintain production and activity at the production license in the northern part of the North Sea. Operator Equinor on Thursday said that together with its partners Petoro and OMV, it had discovered gas at the Gullfaks South field, 190 kilometers (118 miles) northwest of Bergen. articles.title: Oil Prices Rebound Intraday Thursday
articles.description: Naeem Aslam, CIO at Zaye Capital Markets, outlines the main driver.

articles.title: UAE Joins Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan in Push for Trans-Afghan Railway
articles.description: It appears Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan may have found a way to finance a trans-Afghan railway that would enable Central Asian exports to gain access to seaports in Pakistan. Transport officials from the two Central Asian states have signed a memorandum of understanding with the United Arab Emirates covering “the practical development” of the railway, according to a Kazakh government statement. Astana and Tashkent have been strong advocates for a trans-Afghan railway but lack the financial resources and technical expertise…

articles.title: Supertanker Rates Hit Record $1.4 Million a Day
articles.description: The oil crisis has extended into the shipping sector with a large tanker fleet tied up in ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, pushing global freight rates to record highs and reducing vessel availability for other routes. Supertanker rates have soared in recent weeks, and hit a record-high of $1.4 million per day on the Gulf to East Asia trip, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Rates on the U.S. Gulf-to-Japan route are also skyrocketing and one supertanker, the so-called very large crude carrier (VLCC) capable of shipping…

articles.title: Syria Expects to Double Oil Output in a Year
articles.description: State-owned Syria Petroleum expects oil output to increase to about 250,000 barrels a day by the end of 2027 from about 110,000 barrels a day now by investing in existing fields.

articles.title: PCEC, PDVSA agree to revive Venezuela’s Delta and Cabimas fields
articles.description: Pacific Coast Energy Company (PCEC) has entered into agreements with Petróleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) to manage and develop oil fields in the Delta and Cabimas blocks in Venezuela.

articles.title: U.S. and Russia Discuss Reviving Russian Gas Sales to Europe
articles.description: The United States and Russia have discussed the idea of finding a U.S. investor for the Nord Stream pipeline and working out sales of Russian gas to Europe, Reuters reported on Thursday, citing sources with knowledge of recent meetings between top U.S. and Russian officials. U.S. Special Envoy Jared Kushner, son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump, and Kirill Dmitriev, a close adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin and head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund, the sovereign wealth fund, have met in Moscow and New York in recent weeks…

articles.title: Oil Jumps 5% as Iran Steps Up Attacks on Hormuz Tankers
articles.description: Brent crude swung back above $105 per barrel today as reports flow in about increasingly frequent Iranian attacks on tankers in Hormuz while U.S. Gulf Coast operators began shutting in production and prepping refineries ahead of an approaching storm. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $105.02 per barrel, up by over 4.81% from Wednesday’s close... articles.title: India's Inflation Likely Hit 5.4% in September as Oil Costs Bite
articles.description: India’s inflation is estimated to have accelerated to 5.4% in September, up from 4.82% in August, on the back of soaring oil prices and energy and food costs, a Reuters poll of economists showed on Thursday. The forecasts of the 41 economists surveyed by Reuters ranged from 4.9% to as much as 5.9%. Apart from food and beverage inflation, “we are also beginning to see clearer evidence of energy prices spilling over into other parts of the ‌CPI, rather than just transport,” ANZ economist Dhiraj Nim told Reuters. Accelerating…

articles.title: First Deep-Gulf Tanker Attack in Nearly a Month Hits Vessel off Qatar
articles.description: A tanker has been struck by multiple projectiles north of Qatar’s tip in the first such attack deep within the Persian Gulf in nearly a month. A tanker has reported being struck by multiple projectiles 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which is affiliated with the Royal Navy, reported. Casualties have been reported, and authorities are investigating, UKMTO said about the incident, the report of which was received late on Wednesday local time. This is the first reported…

articles.title: Big Oil Begins Shutting In Gulf of Mexico Production
articles.description: Shell and Chevron have started shutting in platforms in the Gulf of Mexico ahead of an approaching storm that could become a hurricane by the end of the week. Shell is evacuating all personnel from five platforms, including Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito, and Appomattox, and shutting production activities there. Chevron, meanwhile, is doing the same at four offshore platforms in the Gulf, but leaving another five platforms operating normally. Earlier reports said BP was also evacuating staff from offshore platforms in the Gulf. Tropical storm Isaias…

articles.title: Hormuz Tanker Traffic Hits Two-Month Low as Attacks Surge
articles.description: The number of tankers traversing the Strait of Hormuz has dropped to the lowest in two months amid renewed attacks on vessels in the waterway—right after tanker-tracking outlets said oil flows out of Hormuz are back to pre-war levels. “Crude crossing the strait fell 27% from a wartime high the week before, to at least 10.1 million barrels a day,” two Kpler analysts reported, as the firm counted only seven commodity carriers traversing the strait on Tuesday.
